subject: Some d parameters missing from output

messages.author: c28cd713d9507032
messages.subject: Some d parameters missing from output
parts:
Hi, 

I ran a confirmatory model for a graded 4-factor scale. My response scale has 7 points, so 6 d parameters are expected for each item. However, some items are missing the d6, and one is even missing the d5 parameter from the output. Why does this happen? I'm suspecting because too little or no people selected these points - the distribution is heavily skewed. Is this the case? And if so, is the interpretation of other parameters still valid under these circumstances?

Thanks in advance!

Here's an example of the code I ran:

fstruct1 <- 'F1  = Soc1, Soc2, Soc3, Soc4
             F2 = Spt1, Spt, Spt3,  Spt4
             F3 = Hyp1, Hyp2, Hyp3, Hyp4
             F4 = Temp1, Temp2, Temp3, Temp4'

mod <-mirt(data[,2:17], fstruct1, itemtype = "graded", method = 'QMCEM')

messages.author: f0b778df34ff370b
messages.subject: Re: Some d parameters missing from output
parts: i would also guess this would happen if no people select certain categories. for example, if for a 7 category item no one selects the lowest category, then it is effectively treated as a 6 category item by mirt and you'll see fewer estimated intercepts than you expect. i don't see any major problem with interpreting the other parameters if this happens, but with a few cautions. if some items have very few people select certain categories, then estimation for some intercepts for that item may be very unstable (look for large-ish standard errors). if you intend to just interpret results for this measurement instrument for a single study, probably fine, but if you wanted to later use such item parameter estimates with a new batch of participants (e.g., for scoring, or a CAT), then it could be problematic (e.g., suppose one of those new participants does select one of the categories that were not selected during calibration).
